title: voice
description: Who you are, what you can actually prove, and how you are allowed to sound. This is the half of taste that a reference corpus can never supply.

one_liner.description: One sentence a stranger could read to know why you specifically are worth listening to.

intersection.description: The 2-4 things you sit at the intersection of. Two is too broad to be a position; five is a personality, not a channel.

should_feel_like.description: One sentence describing how the account should feel to a stranger.

should_not_become.description: The nearby accounts you would hate to be mistaken for. Negative space defines a position faster than positive claims.

proof.description: Everything you can actually back up. The script agent may only make claims that trace to an entry here.

evidence_location.description: Path or URL to the evidence, if it exists yet.

verified.description: True only if you have personally confirmed this is accurate and current.

expires.description: ISO date after which this claim needs rechecking. Rankings and revenue go stale.

what_they_already_know.description: Sets the floor for how much you explain. Getting this wrong is the most common reason a good script is boring.

say.description: Words, phrasings and rhythms that sound like you.

never_say.description: Hard bans. Filler, guru-isms, and any phrasing borrowed from a reference creator.

resource_offer.description: The one thing a comment keyword actually delivers. Leave empty if you have nothing to give yet - a CTA promising a resource you do not have is the fastest way to lose a new audience.

banned_claims.description: Things that are true-ish but you have decided not to say. Legal, employer, NDA, or taste reasons.

used_hooks.description: Every hook you have already published. The script agent treats a repeat as a hard failure. Appended automatically as you ship.

used_ctas.description: Every CTA phrasing already used. Same rule.
